Casablanca. A 1942 wartime romance and espionage thriller set in French Morocco, where an embittered American barkeeper named Rick must choose between love and conscience when his former lover arrives with her freedom fighter husband. The film blends cynicism, moral ambiguity, and one of cinema's most iconic final scenes. Directed by Michael Curtiz and starring Humphrey Bogart as Rick Blaine and Ingrid Bergman as Ilsa Lund, it won the Academy Award for Best Picture in 1944, alongside Best Director and Best Adapted Screenplay. The setting is the Blue Parrot nightclub in Casablanca during the Nazi occupation of France, a hub for refugees and black market deals. The film features the iconic emotional scene where La Marseillaise is sung to drown out Nazi patrons' songs. The ending defies Hollywood convention: Rick sacrifices his love to help Ilsa and her husband Victor Laszlo escape, joining the Resistance himself. Bogart's most famous line comes as his farewell to Ilsa: "Here's looking at you, kid"—an improvised moment that defined the entire film. Through these characters, Casablanca explores conscience and redemption in the face of impossible choices.
